text:
Looking ahead to the 2050s under high emissions, the best match for the farm's future climate is Whitman County, WA. This is a strong match, and all 8 climate models agree. Lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Out of 5 matching areas checked, 1 uses the field's current rotation, which is a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, winter wheat. Other rotations used at the matching places include a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, winter wheat; winter wheat to spring wheat to fallow; and winter wheat to spring wheat to pulses.

Compared to the best match today, the field currently experiences 18 hot days above 32 degrees Celsius per year, whereas Whitman County has 31. The frost-free season is 150 days at the field and 191 days at the match. Afternoon ground temperature in June is 31.9 degrees at the field and 37.6 degrees at the match, while July-August afternoon ground temperature is 37.4 degrees at the field and 44.2 degrees at the match. For soil water in the driest month of September, the field has 16.6 percent and the match has 21.1 percent.

Overall, the future climate brings warmer temperatures and shifting precipitation across the year. These results are based on 3351 farmland cells.
